headline: Death toll from Monday's Ansar Allah ballistic-missile strike on a government security-forces training camp in Shabwa province rises'
dek: Three ballistic missiles hit a training camp Monday; death toll now 73, 200+ injured, 14 missing — among the deadliest single strikes since fighting re-escalated.
sources: Shabwa provincial media office; provincial governor Awad al-Wazir (injured count); Reuters (video verification)
fault_line: 73 dead in one strike — is the Saudi-led coalition's push to retake the strait backfiring?

sections.what_happened: Three ballistic missiles hit a training camp Monday; death toll now 73, 200+ injured, 14 missing — among the deadliest single strikes since fighting re-escalated.
sections.what_verified: Reuters relay via two aggregators; consistent with thetraveler/analysis describing 53+ dead mid-October Shabwa strike.
sections.what_disputed: Saree's claim the camp was Saudi-run unconfirmed by Riyadh; exact casualty split between soldiers/officials unknown.
sections.why_matters: The deadliest single strike of the renewed Yemen war: 73 killed at a training camp as the Saudi-backed push to retake Bab el-Mandeb meets Ansar Allah ballistic missiles.
sections.context: Background: Yemen — UPDATE: death toll from Monday's Ansar Allah ballistic-missile strike on a government security-forces training camp in Shabwa province rises to 73 (provincial media office), 200+ injured, 14 missing. Reuters-verified video showed bodies/injured. Ansar Allah spokesman Saree says camp was run by Saudi forces (unconfirmed by Riyadh).

totw_analysis: Our read: The deadliest single strike of the renewed Yemen war: 73 killed at a training camp as the Saudi-backed push to retake Bab el-Mandeb meets Ansar Allah ballistic missiles. The fault line our audience is arguing over: 73 dead in one strike — is the Saudi-led coalition's push to retake the strait backfiring?
